_description: AMAS Conflict Resolution Example: Same-Tier Conflict
_scenario: A Tier 2 directive supersedes an older Tier 2 operative object only after authenticated provenance and trusted authorization are established.

object_a.content: Project budget: $50,000. Approved by finance committee 2026-02-15.

object_b.content: Use the revised project budget of $75,000 for this task.

resolution.rule_applied: Semantic-role admissibility for behavior; Rule 2 — Explicit Supersession only if a trusted authorizer confirms authority
resolution.reasoning: The supersession metadata is traceable but is not self-authenticating. A conforming resolver must additionally receive a trusted authorization decision establishing that the issuing actor can supersede the older object at this tier/scope. Without that verifier, Rule 2 fails closed. The directive's narrower scope would also prevail under Rule 3 if no supersession claim were present.
resolution.action: Use $75,000 only after the trusted supersession authorizer returns true; otherwise halt/escalate the supersession conflict.

_fallback_note: If two same-tier directives have no authorized supersession, Rule 3 applies only when one explicit scope_path strictly contains the other. If scopes tie, Rule 4 recency applies. If still unresolved, Rule 5 halts/escalates.
